entry.title: Incident: Custom Applications and Bots may not be working as expected
entry.summary: We continue to see custom applications, integrations and workflows working as expected. We consider the Events API issue resolved, and would like to share some additional detail:Due to mitigation efforts, our Events API built up a considerable backlog of events that were not delivered as expected to apps. Once the database tier became available, we re-enabled these queues and by 11:27pm PST on 2025-02-26, all events were being properly delivered as expected. We chose to not replay the large number of events for delivery that were buffered from the incident because app event delivery semantics often depend on timely delivery for correctness. In addition we wanted to avoid potentially overloading either our systems or those of third-party systems with the surge of queued events which had been paused throughout the outage.We thank you for your patience as we worked through resolution efforts, and we apologize for the disruption caused.

entry.title: Outage: Trouble loading or using Slack
entry.summary: From 6:45 AM PST to 4:13 PM PST on February 26, 2025, a large percentage of Slack users experienced issues with various features including sending and receiving messages, using workflows, loading channels or threads, and logging into Slack. These features may have been degraded or in some cases fully unusable. We traced this issue to a maintenance action in one of our database systems, which, combined with a latency defect in our caching system, caused an overload of heavy traffic to the database. As a result, approximately 50% of instances relying on this database became unavailable. We took several actions to reduce the heavy load on the database system and implemented a fix for the source of the load. At around 9:32 AM PST, we observed improved health metrics for some affected Slack features and at around 4:13 PM PST, our health metrics returned to normal rates, indicating the issue was resolved for all affected users.Edit: After the main impact of this issue was resolved, users experienced issues with our Events API - specifically related to custom applications, integrations and bots not working. This issue is now resolved and these are functioning as expected. You can review specific updates on this resolution here: https://slack-status.com/2025-02/d41e4bfd1ccae26a.

entry.title: Booking.com - Introducing clearer fee & tax breakdown for your reservations
entry.summary:
New!
We’re excited to announce our integration with a new Booking.com’s API, bringing you clearer insights into each reservation’s fees and taxes. Those new informations are available for all Property Managers using Payment by booking (with VCC and Bank transfer), whether you’re using partial or full sync with Booking.com. What’s New? Detailed price breakdown: You’ll now see clearer information on rental fees, cleaning fees, service charges, and city taxes directly in the reservation details as below;
Withheld tax details: In regions where Booking.com withholds tax on your behalf, you’ll see exactly how much was withheld and paid to authorities.
Current balance & VCC info: More visibility on the Virtual Credit Card (VCC) balance, plus its activation and expiration dates.
How Does this affect you? Depending on how Booking.com handles the city tax for each reservation, you’ll see one of these scenarios: 1- Booking.com collects and remits city tax directly to the authorities: Your payment bar will show two payments (one for the rental and one for the withheld tax).
Since Booking.com pays the tax on your behalf, the payment bar will appear “complete.” 2- Booking.com collects the city tax from the guest and includes it in the VCC; you are responsible for remitting the tax: The city tax is included in your total payout, so the payment bar will also appear “complete.”
Don’t forget to pay the tax to your local authorities.
3- Booking.com does not collect the city tax; you must collect and remit it yourself: The payment bar will show the rental amount only (city tax is missing).
You must collect the city tax from guests at check-in and pay it to the authorities.
The city tax is missing from the payment bar, you should collect it before/on check-in.
-> Automatic payment link should be disabled in these cases, Booking.com does not include it in the payment because of regulations. If you have any questions, please reach out to us 🙂 Your Smily team!

entry.title: Incident with Packages
entry.summary: Feb 25, 01:08 UTC Resolved - On February 25, 2025, between 00:17 UTC and 01:08 UTC, GitHub Packages experienced a service degradation, leading to failures uploading and downloading packages, along with increased latency for all requests to GitHub Packages registry. At peak impact, about 14% of uploads and downloads failed, and all Packages requests were delayed by an average of 7 seconds. The incident was caused by the rollout of a database configuration change that resulted in a degradation in database performance. We mitigated the incident by rolling back the contributing change and failing over the database. In response to this incident, we are tuning database configurations and resolving a source of deadlocks. We are also redistributing certain workloads to read replicas to reduce latency and enhance overall database performance. entry.title: Incident with GIT LFS and Other Requests
entry.summary:
Feb 6, 11:13 UTC Resolved - On February 6, 2025, between 8:40AM UTC and 11:13AM UTC the GitHub REST API was degraded following the rollout of a new feature. The feature resulted in an increase in requests that saturated a cache and led to cascading failures in unrelated services. The error rate peaked at 100% of requests to the service. The incident was mitigated by increasing the allocated memory to the cache and rolling back the feature that led to the cache saturation. To prevent future incidents, we are working to reduce the time to detect a similar issue and optimize the overall calls to the cache.
Feb 6, 11:13 UTC Update - This issue has been mitigated. We will continue to investigate root causes to ensure this does not reoccur. entry.title: New booking.com Self-Service messages in Smily
entry.summary:
New!
We’ve enabled Booking.com self-service requests directly in the Smily PMS inbox! 🎉 When guests send special requests (extra bed, early check-in, etc.) during or after their booking, these requests will appear directly in your Smily inbox. 📩 Requests include: check-in/out time, date change, free cancellation, parking, bed preference, extra crib, extra bed 💡 What does this mean for you? 1️⃣ Monitor your Smily inbox to see potential guest requests from Booking.com. These messages will appear just like regular messages. 2️⃣ Choose where to respond: ✅ If you want to continue using Booking.com’s automation, reply via the Extranet using the quick-response options like below ⬇️
✍️ If you prefer to handle the request manually, reply with free text in Smily. (⚠️ This will end the automated flow for that request.) 3️⃣ Be vigilant with cancellations and date changes 📆 These will always be sent as free text and will require manual action on your part. 🔎 Important clarifications 1️⃣ Quick-response options (as shown above) are only available on the Booking.com Extranet Guests can submit their self-service requests (e.g., “Extra bed request,” “Check-in time change”), and you will see these new messages in Smily.
However, you cannot use the quick-response buttons (e.g., “Confirm for free,” “Confirm with charges,” etc.) from Smily. 👉 If you want to use these buttons, you must do so via the Booking.com Extranet. In Smily, you can only respond with a free-text message. ✍️ 2️⃣ No automated cancellations or date changes No booking is automatically cancelled or modified unless the guest does it themselves via Booking.com or you process it manually. Make sure to confirm any cancellation or date change request yourself! 💬 Any questions? Need help? Our support team is here for you! 🚀💙

entry.title: Incident: Slowness searching with Slack AI
entry.summary: Issue Summary:From 6:30 PM PST on January 28, 2025 to around 11:00 AM PST on January 30, 2025, some Slack AI customers may have experienced issues with Slack AI searches.A configuration issue with some of our Slack AI infrastructure resulted in an unexpected backlog of Slack AI tasks. This backlog meant that Slack AI responses were not served to users in a timely manner. Additionally, certain Slack AI queries had very long timeout windows, remaining in the queue indefinitely and contributing to the backlog. We scaled up our Slack AI infrastructure to increase our capacity to work through the backlog and manually ended any stuck queries. We also deployed a code change to set more reasonable timeout windows for the long-running queries, resolving the issue for all impacted users.
